title: Throughput Sensitivity Sprint Planning - Observability & Serving
body:
Context:
We observed a slow, but consistent, increase in end-to-end p99 latency for high token-length requests (>=4096 tokens) across a small subset of Dedicated pools after the kernel selector rollout (kernel-v1.3.2) on 2025-10-01. This doc captures the observability team sync on 2025-10-07 to plan a focused sprint: reproduce, isolate, and propose mitigations for throughput sensitivity and latency drift.

Attendees:
- Aisha Patel (owner)
- Marco Li (serving-runtime)
- Devika Rao (perf-eng)
- Samir Khan (SRE)
- Ellen Brooks (QA / e2e)

Summary of current signals:
- Canary cluster (eu-west-1-dedicated-42) shows p50 stable, p95 up 8-12ms, p99 up 25-40ms for requests with sequence lengths in 4k-8k range.
- CPU scheduling stalls correlated with larger KV-cache RTs in traces (samples attached in Confluence).
- Increased retry rate observed for batch sizes > 12 when autoscaler attempts to pack more concurrent sessions.
- No increase in token-generation error codes; content quality unaffected.

Repro matrix run (Devika):
- Baseline: model xlm-4b-q8a, batch sizes [1,4,8,12,16], seq lens [512,2048,4096,8192] on kernel-v1.2.9.
- New test: same matrix on kernel-v1.3.2.
- Results: divergence appears at batch >=8 and seq >=4096. Throughput drops ~18% and p99 increases as noted.
- Raw result artifacts: see linked_artifacts.

Hypotheses brainstormed:
1) Kernel change increased context-switch overhead for continuous batching path (serving-runtime).
2) KV cache eviction policy interacts poorly with new memory allocator leading to transient async stalls (platform infra).
3) Autoscaler packing logic pushes too many sessions into a single worker when latency variance increases, worsening tail latency.

Immediate action plan (owners + ETA):
- A1: Re-run focused microbench with KV cache instrumentation enabled on kernel-v1.3.2 vs v1.2.9 to capture eviction/alloc traces. Owner: Devika. ETA: 2025-10-09.
- A2: Add lightweight tracing hook to serving-runtime batching loop to log time spent in queue->dispatch path for batch sizes 8/12/16. Owner: Marco. ETA: 2025-10-10.
- A3: Temporarily restrict autoscaler packing policy for canary pool to max concurrent per-worker = 10 to see if tail improves. Owner: Samir. ETA: 2025-10-08 (change deployed to canary).
- A4: QA run synthetic e2e with user-like prompt mixes (dense long responses) and collect p99/p999. Owner: Ellen. ETA: 2025-10-11.
- A5: Create A/B rollback plan for kernel selector if regressions confirmed and mitigations not effective within 72 hours. Owner: Aisha. ETA: 2025-10-08 for plan.

Metrics to capture during experiments:
- p50/p95/p99/p999 for token ranges 512/2048/4096/8192
- worker CPU-steal and migration counts (SRE)
- KV cache hit/miss/eviction latency histograms
- batching queue wait time distribution
- throughput (tokens/sec and requests/sec) and retry rates

Notes from discussion:
- Devika: initial microbench suggests a 10-12ms overhead in the batching dispatch call on v1.3.2; unclear if allocator or kernel shim added syscall latency.
- Marco: will instrument with sub-ms timers and correlate with kernel traces; avoid heavy sampling that skews results.
- Samir: deploy packing change to canary by EOD; will monitor for regression on cost-efficiency but prioritize tail improvement.
- Ellen: e2e harness needs an updated prompt corpus reflecting the new long-response benchmark; will reuse last quarter's corpus with added adversarial long-turn prompts.

Open questions / risks:
- Risk: pack-change reduces throughput efficiency and increases GPU count needed for same load if long-term. Need to quantify.
- Q: Does kernel selector provide a fallback to previous kernel for affected workloads automatically? Aisha to confirm with release-engineering.
- Q: Could quantization profile differences cause increased KV cache pressure? Mark for follow-up with model-onboarding.

Decisions made:
- Short-term: restrict packing on canary; run microbench and tracing; prioritize p99 reduction over packing efficiency for the canary window.
- Mid-term: if root cause is allocator/kernel, prepare rollback or targeted patch with release-engineering and perf team.

Next steps / meeting cadence:
- Daily short standups at 09:30 PT during active experiments (channel: #perf-throughput-sprint).
- Full sync on 2025-10-09 11:00 PT to review Devika + Marco findings and decide on rollback.

Reference artifacts and quick links:
- GitHub PR with proposed batching instrumentation: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/4821
- Jira ticket tracking: INFER-2147 (throughput sensitivity after kernel selector rollout)
- Confluence runbook & raw traces: OBS/Throughput-Sensitivity-Runbook (internal link)

Notes-to-self (informal):
- Keep kernel-v1.2.9 baseline snapshots around for quick repros; tag AMIs and worker configs.
- Save sample traces from canary cluster with high p99 to S3 path: s3://redwood-observability/canary/2025-10-07/samples/
- Remember to coordinate rollback windows with infra maintenance to avoid concurrency with other migrations.

Action item summary (short):
- Devika: KV cache microbench w/ alloc traces (ETA 10/09)
- Marco: batching loop timers + trace correlation (ETA 10/10)
- Samir: deploy packing limit to canary + monitor (done 10/08)
- Ellen: e2e corpus update + run (ETA 10/11)
- Aisha: rollback plan and release-eng confirmation (ETA 10/08)

End of notes.
